headline: High: Roo Code’s broad filesystem, shell, MCP, and browser access can conflict with a non-runnable content-only peer, creating default workspace and downstream-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no runnable tool surface or shared channel beyond being a content-writing artifact, while B can read/write the VS Code workspace and use MCP. The only plausible bridge is manual or workspace-mediated copy, so injection is possible but not default and blast radius is limited by the lack of an executable A surface.
conditions: IF A’s content is copied into B’s workspace or MCP-fed prompt, B may ingest attacker-controlled instructions.
IF B is configured to treat workspace text as trusted instructions, prompt injection becomes feasible.
mitigations: Keep A outputs out of B’s instruction channel.
Use a strict prompt/template separator for any copied text.
Disable MCP tools for untrusted content review sessions.
Review B’s system prompt for instruction/data delimiters.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B has broad filesystem read/write and broad network egress, so any sensitive workspace content can leave the machine through B’s model/API or browser paths. A is content-only and does not itself touch sensitive data, but its outputs can be placed into B’s workspace; the pair therefore creates a default leakage path once sensitive files are present.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared VS Code workspace, B can read them.
IF B sends workspace context to a configured model API or MCP server, those contents may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Restrict B to a scrubbed workspace.
Remove secrets before opening the workspace in B.
Disable network egress for review-only sessions.
Use separate OS users for A and B workflows.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or execution capability, so it cannot directly contend for mutable resources. B can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses in a workspace-scoped concurrency model, so conflicts arise if both are pointed at the same repo or files; uncertainty is low because A’s lack of mutability is explicit.
conditions: IF both agents are assigned the same workspace or git repository, B can overwrite or race on files.
IF A is used only as a read-only content source, direct capability conflict remains limited.
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces.
Pause B before any git-write step.
Use branch-per-agent workflows.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a content-writing source and B is a coding agent that can act on workspace content, so A’s outputs can become B’s inputs without a built-in verification barrier. Because B has shell, browser, and git actions, a mistaken or malicious A output can cascade into code changes or external actions; this is a default interaction risk, not merely unusual configuration.
conditions: IF B uses A’s text as authoritative guidance, errors can propagate into code or commits.
IF B is allowed to execute shell or git actions based on A’s output, downstream impact increases.
mitigations: Require B to verify A outputs against source material.
Add a human approval step before commits or shell execution.
Mark A outputs as untrusted drafts.
Use checklists for any action derived from A text.

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for A, while B handles source code and browser screenshots and may send them to configured model APIs. Because the pairwise compliance pathway is undocumented and A is not a regulated-data agent, the main issue is a generic policy gap rather than a proven breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into B’s workspace or browser screenshots, external transmission may violate local policy.
IF B is configured with a third-party model API lacking an appropriate DPA, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B sessions.
Disable screenshot capture when unnecessary.
Use approved model endpoints only.
Document retention and deletion rules for workspace artifacts.
